decision_log.decision: Complete T29 common-cause sensor reference and supplement-actuator fault experiment; require shadow-balance and actuator-meter residuals alongside pairwise sensor disagreement before relying on automated supplement fallback; keep qualification hold in force until multi-unit shared-service contention and biological validation exist
decision_log.rationale: T28 established that pairwise sensor disagreement catches single-sensor bias and dropout, but left shared-reference common-mode sensor faults and supplement-actuator offsets untested. T29 demonstrates on the same whole-path twin that pairwise disagreement detects 0/7 common-sensor-bias samples and 0/7 actuator-offset samples, whereas augmenting disagreement with a shadow bulk-balance residual and metered-actuator residual detects all three fault classes (4/6, 5/7, 5/7 samples with 0 false alarms) and isolates the actuator offset while internal tissue-use and progression states remain structurally unobservable from boundary/bulk channels.

decision_log.decision: Complete T30 multi-unit shared-service contention experiment; demonstrate that a fault in unit A propagates to unit B through a shared bulk stock reservoir, and that per-unit boundary monitoring cannot distinguish cross-unit propagation from local delivery failure. Isolated operation eliminates cross-unit propagation but does not represent the shared-infrastructure architecture. Keep qualification hold until multi-unit physical testbed and biological validation exist.
decision_log.rationale: T29 established that pairwise sensor disagreement misses common-cause faults within a single unit. T30 extends the fault register to cross-unit propagation: when two units share a common resource, a fault in one unit can degrade the other through resource depletion, and the degraded unit's boundary observables cannot distinguish this from its own local failure. This has direct consequences for the ten-unit shared-infrastructure architecture: per-unit monitoring alone is insufficient to diagnose cross-unit resource contention.

tasks.decision_consequence: Qualifies that pairwise sensor disagreement (`|primary - secondary|`) is structurally blind to shared-reference common-mode sensor bias and downstream supplement-actuator offsets (`0/7` fault samples detected in each window), whereas coupling pairwise disagreement with a shadow bulk-balance residual and metered-actuator residual detects all three fault classes (`4/6`, `5/7`, `5/7` samples after 2-sample confirmation with `0` false alarms), latches frozen-supplement fallback, and isolates the actuator offset without claiming visibility into hidden internal tissue or progression failure.

Dimensionless whole-path common-cause sensor and supplement-actuator fault module

Eleven regression tests for common-cause blindness of pairwise disagreement, balance/actuator detection, T21/T28 equivalence, hidden internal-state invariance, and input/work-budget guards

tasks.stop_rule: Do not treat shadow-balance or actuator-meter residuals as biological safety, multi-unit physical isolation, or internal tissue-use observability; keep the qualification hold until multi-unit shared-service contention and biological validation exist.

tasks.acceptance: Publish a dimensionless multi-unit shared-reservoir contention module (src/wombmodels/multi_unit_contention.py, examples/multi_unit_contention_fixture.json, CLI multi-unit-contention-model, bundle kind dimensionless_multi_unit_contention) that runs two gestation units sharing a common bulk stock reservoir, applies sensor_bias and actuator_offset faults to unit A only, and tests cross-unit propagation through the shared resource while preserving exact isolated-to-T21 trajectory equality and verifying that unit B's boundary channels cannot distinguish shared-reservoir depletion from local delivery failure.
tasks.decision_consequence: Qualifies that a fault in one unit propagates to another through a shared resource (shared reservoir), that per-unit boundary monitoring cannot distinguish cross-unit propagation from local failure, and that isolated operation eliminates cross-unit propagation by construction. This does not establish physical multi-unit isolation, fluidic testbed capability or biological safety.
